# What to expect from this course

## What does GAPS say (1/3)

- [Fiche d'unité](https://heigvd-dai-26.github.io/resources.html) (2026-2027)
- Three (3) ECTS credits (~90 hours of work):
  - 64 periods of 45 minutes (= 48 hours in class).
  - The rest outside class. We do our best to keep it reasonable.

> **Connaissances préalables recommandées** : programmation (Java, C) ;
> programmation orientée objet ; TCP/IP.
> Les unités PRG2, RXI et POO permettent d'acquérir ces connaissances.

## What does GAPS say (2/3)

> **Programmation réseau**
>
> - concevoir une application client-serveur ;
> - implémenter un client et un serveur en utilisant la Socket API dans
>   différents langages ;
>
> **Protocole HTTP**
>
> - connaître les concepts principaux du protocole ;
> - concevoir et réaliser une infrastructure HTTP avec un reverse proxy et
>   plusieurs serveurs ;

## What does GAPS say (3/3)

> **Protocoles de messagerie**
>
> - connaître les principaux protocoles relatifs à la messagerie
>   électronique ;
> - implémenter un client de messagerie simple ;
>
> **Protocoles de transfert de fichiers et d'accès à distance**
>
> - connaître ces protocoles et leurs principales utilisations (y compris
>   tunneling/forwarding).

## Topics

- Network programming (inputs/outputs, encodings, TCP and UDP).
- Application-level protocols (SMTP, SSH, HTTP, and your own).
- Web infrastructures (reverse proxy, load balancer, sticky sessions).
- How to read and write technical documentation.

At the end of the course, you will be able to create applications that
communicate over the network: business applications, APIs, games, etc.!

## Technologies

- Git and GitHub.
- Markdown.
- Java for network programming.
- Docker & Docker Compose.
- Network utilities.
- The terminal.

## Why do you have this course

- Defines the basics of network communication and how these
  communications are programmed.
- You will know how to define, program and deploy network applications,
  and what makes them robust.
- Software, security, data science, embedded or networking: you **will**
  deal with network applications (APIs, devices, services).

# How the course works

## Program (1/2)

The teaching unit is divided in 3 main parts:

- Part 1: Input/output processing.
- Part 2: Network programming with TCP and UDP.
- Part 3: Network programming with HTTP.

The entire week-by-week program is available on the
[course site](https://heigvd-dai-26.github.io/).

## Program (2/2)

- Dates are based on the
  [HEIG-VD academic calendar](https://heig-vd.ch/formation/bachelor/calendrier-academique/).
- **The program is subject to change.**
- We will do our best to inform you in advance if there are any changes.

## Course sequence

1. Short and concise overview of each subject (20–30 minutes).
2. Practice the content: exercises with solutions in each chapter.
3. Practical works: **freedom of subject**, you choose what you build.
4. Feedback and discussions: very important to us.

## Grading

- Three (3) practical works, in groups: **20%** (labo grade).
- Two (2) evaluations, individually: **80%** (cours grade):
  - TE1 (mid-term) 40% · TE2 (final) 60%.
- No exam session. Everything happens during the semester.

You can change groups between practical works. We try to return grades
and feedback quickly, and we can be flexible on deadlines, with a good
reason.

## Communication channels

- Email, with the whole teaching staff in copy:
  - [olivier.tischhauser@heig-vd.ch](mailto:olivier.tischhauser@heig-vd.ch)
  - [cedric.camposcarvalho@heig-vd.ch](mailto:cedric.camposcarvalho@heig-vd.ch)

## Where to find the course material

**Everything** is on the course site:

- <https://heigvd-dai-26.github.io/>

No Microsoft Teams, no CyberLearn: one place to find it all.

Spotted something weird? Issues and pull requests are welcome. 🙂

# Our wishes for this course

## What we want this course to be

- A place to learn.
- A place to experiment, where it is OK to make mistakes.
- A place to share and discuss.
- A place where you are able to do things and master them.
- A place where you can express your opinion.
- It is OK if you are not feeling well. We are here if you need to talk.
- A place where you do not lose your time.

## What we don't want this course to be

- A place you don't want to come to.
- A place you don't feel comfortable or safe.
- A place where you can't ask questions or make mistakes.
- A place where you can't take anything away.

If you have a problem with the course, we will do our best to fix it.

If you are done, you are free to go, but helping your classmates is
appreciated!

## Responsibilities and expectations

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Ours**

- You acquire the knowledge of this course.
- You are prepared for the professional world.
- Your feedback is taken into account.
- We are available and give useful feedback.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Yours**

- Read and understand the course material.
- Do the practical contents.
- You are responsible for your own learning: ask, tell us, suggest.
:::

## *"Un cours en anglais..?"*

- Written material in **English**, the language of the field. A great
  opportunity to practice.
- The teaching staff speaks **French**. Evaluations are in **French**.
- Difficulties with English? Let us know.

## *"What about ChatGPT, Copilot, Claude…?"* (1/2)

**You can use the tools you want, responsibly and within the
[guidelines set by the school](https://heigvd-dai-26.github.io/resources/ia-principes-heig-vd.pdf)**,
except during the evaluations.

They can help you, but they are not a replacement for your own knowledge
and skills: focus on understanding first, then let the tools help with
the implementation.

## *"What about ChatGPT, Copilot, Claude…?"* (2/2)

The rules:

- You **must be able to explain what you did and why**.
- You **must state when you used external help** (tools and sources).
- You **must be able to do the work on your own**. Tools come and go.

**Your personal and scientific integrity is at stake.** If we have
doubts, we will ask you to explain your work.

## *"Linux, macOS or Windows?"*

- Software development on Windows is harder: use **WSL**. Chapter 00
  guides you through it.
- On macOS: **Homebrew** for the tooling, also in chapter 00.
- Whatever the OS: **every verification in
  [chapter 00](https://heigvd-dai-26.github.io/chapters/00-environment-setup.html)
  must pass.**

ARM computer (Apple Silicon)? Mostly fine. Tell us as soon as something
misbehaves.
